claims.text: Tribological performance of HEA coatings initially improves as ambient temperature rises, with an optimum at 200–400 °C.
The intermediate-temperature improvement is caused by adaptive, self-lubricating oxide tribo-layers.
Tribological performance degrades above approximately 400–500 °C.
Excessive oxidation at high temperature increases wear.
High-temperature phase instability and coating-matrix softening increase wear and may cause galling.
An AlCoCrFeNiTi coating can be deposited on 316 stainless steel by atmospheric plasma spraying.
CoCrFeMnNi and (CoCrFeMnNi)85Ti15 coatings have been formed on Q235 steel by plasma cladding and studied under high-temperature friction and wear conditions.
CuMoTaWV is among the metallic high-entropy coating systems considered in the literature.
High-entropy coatings can be fabricated using atmospheric plasma spraying, laser or plasma cladding, and related thermal-spray methods.
The proposed coatings exhibit multiphase microstructures containing solid-solution or intermetallic phases.
Relevant sliding tests span 25–600 °C, 0.5–2 m/s, 5–20 N, and 500–2000 m in air.
Si3N4, Al2O3, or steel counterfaces are applicable to the proposed ball-on-disk or pin-on-disk tests.
V2O5-, CuO-, or Cr2O3-rich tribo-layers act as solid lubricants at intermediate temperatures.
High configurational entropy and slow diffusion in HEAs promote selective oxidation of V, Cu, or Cr at temperatures up to 400 °C.
The selectively formed oxides constitute protective, low-shear-strength tribo-layers that reduce friction and wear.
Above 400 °C, tribo-layers become unstable and produce thick brittle scales, oxide spallation, phase decomposition, and matrix softening.
Oxide spallation, phase decomposition, and matrix softening accelerate abrasive and adhesive wear.
The coefficient of friction decreases from room temperature to approximately 300 °C and then rises above 400 °C.
Wear rate follows a U-shaped temperature dependence, with a minimum at 200–400 °C and a sharp increase above 400–500 °C.
Conventional NiCrBSi coatings show monotonic degradation in wear resistance with temperature because they lack adaptive tribo-layers and have lower thermal stability.
